title: consolidate-retry-choreography-and-handshake-shims-across-py-ts-go-sdks
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Introduce unified RetryProfile and lightweight stream handshake adapters across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs. Bug fixes for stream resume and token refresh ergonomics. Bump SDK versions: py v1.39.0, ts v1.28.0, go v1.8.0.
description:
Context and motivation: Our three SDKs had slightly divergent retry/backoff defaults and streaming handshake behavior which led to subtle production differences (session churn, spurious reconnects, and auth edgecases). This PR centralizes the retry choreography model (RetryProfile), surfaces a compact, polymorphic handshake shim for streaming consumers, and aligns default ergonomics so parity tests and customer integrations behave consistently across languages.

What changed (high level):
- Introduce RetryProfile (language-agnostic spec + local translators) and wire it into existing retry logic for HTTP and streaming codepaths.
- Add HandshakeShim: a minimal stream handshake adapter that centralizes reauth, preflight, and resume token exchange semantics used by all three SDKs.
- Replace per-SDK ad-hoc backoff code with translators that convert a RetryProfile into SDK-native settings (jitter strategy, max_attempts, per-stage timeouts).
- Ergonomic API tweaks: Python and TS add Stream.handle() convenience wrapper that returns a typed async generator with automatic resume; Go adds PullStream.Interface with the same semantics.
- Bump SDK versions for release and update changelogs.

Commits (summary):
- f1a2b3c: add RetryProfile spec and Rust reference serializer used by test harness
- d4e5f6a: implement translator and slot mappings for Python SDK
- c7d8e9f: TS: handshake shim + stream.handle() wrapper + docs update
- a0b1c2d: Go: PullStream interface + translator + unit tests
- e3f4g5h: align CI matrix, add cross-sdk parity tests, fix flakey timeouts

- sdk/python/redwood/streaming/handshake_shim.py (new)
- sdk/python/tests/test_retry_profiles.py (new parity tests)

Review conversation (high-level):
- Ethan Liu: "Looks great overall; left a couple nits about the RetryProfile naming and an edgecase in the jitter math for exponential backoff at high attempt counts."
- Maya (author): "Addressed the jitter bounds, added a comment describing rationale. Also added a small test to guard against overflow in the schedule computation."
- Sofia Gomez: "Can we avoid changing the public SDK constructor signatures in this PR? We should keep compatibility surface minimal."
- Maya: "Kept a thin compatibility shim: new constructors are additive and old signatures delegate to the compatibility path. Added unit tests exercising both."
- Liam O'Connor: "CI showed flake in py integration harness on first run, looks unrelated but re-run required."

CI and testing:
- Initial run (2026-02-20): Found a flaky test in python integration (test_stream_resume) — likely timing-dependent.
- Fix and retry: tightened test to use deterministic clock and added a retry guard. Re-ran CI.
- Final status: All checks green across py/ts/go matrices, parity suite passed on the matrix runner.

Compatibility notes and rollout plan:
- No breaking changes: public constructors are additive. For teams that previously relied on implicit backoff defaults, behavior may change slightly (more consistent across SDKs); we documented the mapping and provided an opt-out to keep legacy defaults.
- Rollout: staged release — publish SDK prereleases to npm/pypi/go proxy, run a small internal canary on Dedicated and Hosted API, monitor session churn and token refresh metrics for 72 hours before promoting.

Follow-ups (short list):
- ENG-4922: Harvest telemetry for RetryProfile decisions and expose a console toggle to prefer legacy or unified profiles.
- SDK-113: Deprecate legacy per-sdk backoff helpers in a minor release after users have had time to opt-in.

Why this is different from prior PRs: Previous work focused on localized retry ergonomics (per-SDK). This PR creates a cross-language canonical model (RetryProfile) and a compact handshake surface that reduces duplication and makes policy changes (e.g., change to jitter strategy) deployable consistently across customers and runtimes.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged to main after approvals from Ethan and Sofia and CI green. Changelog and release artifacts updated; npm/pypi/go releases staged.
